stories.title: XRP ETFs extend crypto's longest active daily inflow streak
stories.summary: XRP-linked ETFs are on the longest continuous run of daily net inflows of any crypto ETF product currently trading, according to CryptoSlate. The streak stands out because several rival crypto ETFs have been struggling to attract fresh money over the same period.
stories.whyItMatters: Sustained inflows into a single altcoin ETF product while peers stall suggests institutional demand is becoming more selective within crypto ETFs rather than spreading evenly across the sector.
whatToWatch: Whether the inflow streak continues or breaks in the coming days
Whether competing crypto ETFs see inflows recover
questions: What is driving demand specifically toward XRP ETF products right now?
How long can the streak realistically extend?

sources.title: XRP extends the longest active ETF inflow streak in crypto as rival funds struggle for fresh cash

stories.title: Suspected fourth Coldcard attack wave drains 389 BTC, Galaxy analyst says
stories.summary: A suspected fourth wave of attacks tied to the ongoing Coldcard hardware wallet exploit swept an additional 389 BTC, according to Galaxy's Thorn as reported by Cointelegraph. This adds to prior waves of losses already linked to the same vulnerability.
stories.whyItMatters: Repeated attack waves against the same hardware wallet flaw indicate the exploit remains active and unmitigated, a serious concern for holders who rely on hardware wallets as a security baseline.
whatToWatch: Whether additional attack waves are detected
Any official response or patch from Coldcard
Running tally of total funds drained
questions: Has the underlying vulnerability been patched?
Who is behind the attacks, and are they linked across waves?

sources.title: Suspected 4th Coldcard attack wave sweeps 389 Bitcoin: Galaxy’s Thorn

stories.title: ZeroStack's crypto stash shrinks from $163M to $15M, leaving it to lean on staking rewards
stories.summary: ZeroStack's crypto holdings have collapsed from roughly $163 million to about $15 million, according to CryptoSlate, pushing the firm to rely on staking rewards to sustain itself. The report does not specify the exact cause of the decline.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a stark illustration of how quickly a crypto-heavy treasury can deteriorate, adding to a growing list of cautionary cases for firms leaning on token holdings as a core strategy.
whatToWatch: Whether staking income is sufficient to stabilize the firm
Any further disclosures on what caused the drop
questions: Was the collapse driven by price declines, withdrawals, or something else?
Is ZeroStack at risk of insolvency?

sources.title: This $163M crypto stash collapsed to just $15M, forcing ZeroStack to literally stake its survival on token rewards

stories.title: Hodler's Digest: Coldcard exploit drives Bitcoin to safer wallets amid 'bullish' consolidation talk
stories.summary: Cointelegraph's weekly Hodler's Digest recap for August 2 centers on the Coldcard exploit prompting holders to move Bitcoin to safety, alongside commentary framing the recent price consolidation as bullish. As a roundup, it aggregates the week's notable crypto developments rather than reporting a single new event.
stories.whyItMatters: Digest coverage reflects how the Coldcard exploit is shaping broader market sentiment and behavior beyond just direct victims.
whatToWatch: Whether the 'bullish consolidation' read holds up in coming sessions
questions: How much of recent BTC movement is exploit-driven versus organic trading?

stories.title: Interactive Strength wipes out $50M FET token bet, subordinates common shareholders
stories.summary: Interactive Strength has erased a $50 million bet on FET tokens gone wrong, and in the process restructured its capital stack so common shareholders now sit behind other claims, per CryptoSlate. Details on how the token position failed were not specified beyond the write-down.
stories.whyItMatters: It's another example of a public company's crypto treasury bet backfiring and directly affecting shareholder standing, a risk investors in crypto-exposed equities should weigh.
whatToWatch: Further company disclosures on the restructuring terms
Stock price and investor reaction
questions: What exactly caused the FET token bet to fail?
What recourse, if any, do common shareholders have?

sources.title: How Interactive Strength erased a $50M FET token bet and sent common shareholders to the back of the line

stories.title: Another crypto wallet is shutting down tomorrow with no firm cutoff time, prompting a scramble to move funds
stories.summary: A crypto wallet provider is set to shut down as early as tomorrow without a precise cutoff time, according to CryptoSlate, leaving users racing to withdraw or migrate their tokens before losing access. It's described as the latest in a string of similar wallet shutdowns.
stories.whyItMatters: Abrupt wallet shutdowns underscore the operational and custodial risks users face even outside of hacks, especially when exit windows are vague.
whatToWatch: The actual shutdown time once confirmed
Whether affected users successfully retrieve their funds
questions: Which wallet provider is shutting down, and why?
What happens to funds users fail to move in time?

sources.title: Another crypto wallet pulls the plug tomorrow with no exact cutoff, leaving users racing to rescue tokens

stories.title: Real estate firm bets $8M on crypto it may not be able to withdraw, after three reverse splits and a $13.5M loss
stories.summary: A real estate company that has undergone three reverse stock splits and posted a $13.5 million loss has put $8 million into crypto, per CryptoSlate, though restrictions may prevent it from withdrawing the funds. The report does not name the specific asset or detail the exact withdrawal restrictions.
stories.whyItMatters: It fits a pattern of financially struggling public companies turning to crypto treasury bets as a lifeline, which can carry outsized risk for existing shareholders.
whatToWatch: Whether withdrawal terms are clarified in future filings
Stock performance following the disclosure
questions: What crypto asset did the firm buy?
What specifically restricts its ability to withdraw?

sources.title: After 3 reverse stock splits and a $13.5M loss, this real estate firm bet $8M on crypto it may not be allowed to withdraw

stories.title: Small cluster of Solana bots gains 3x trading edge via proprietary routing protocol
stories.summary: A small group of Solana trading bots secured roughly a 3x trading advantage by routing orders through a single proprietary protocol, according to CryptoSlate. The report doesn't name the protocol or quantify how many traders are affected market-wide.
stories.whyItMatters: It points to uneven access to execution advantages on Solana, relevant to ongoing concerns about MEV and fairness in on-chain trading.
whatToWatch: Whether the protocol involved is publicly identified
Any response from Solana ecosystem participants or validators
questions: Which protocol is being used, and is access restricted to a few bots?
Could this advantage be replicated or countered by other traders?

sources.title: A tiny cluster of Solana bots unlocked a 3x trading advantage by routing through one proprietary protocol

stories.title: Coldcard wallet bug tied to $89M in Bitcoin movement, the largest since FTX
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports the Coldcard wallet vulnerability has now been linked to roughly $89 million in Bitcoin movement, marking the largest such shift since the FTX collapse and reportedly muddying on-chain market signals in the process.
stories.whyItMatters: A hardware wallet flaw large enough to distort broader market data shows how security incidents can ripple beyond direct victims into market analytics.
whatToWatch: Whether the tally continues to grow
How analysts adjust on-chain signal readings to account for the distortion
questions: How much of the $89M reflects attacker activity versus precautionary user transfers?

sources.title: Coldcard’s $89M wallet bug triggers the biggest Bitcoin movement since FTX and completely distorts market signals

stories.title: Coldcard Bitcoin exploit total climbs to $88M as attackers keep draining wallets
stories.summary: Decrypt reports the Coldcard Bitcoin wallet exploit has grown to an estimated $88 million as attackers continue draining affected wallets. The figure is still being tracked as the incident unfolds.
stories.whyItMatters: A climbing loss total signals the exploit is ongoing rather than contained, raising the stakes for Coldcard users who haven't yet secured their holdings.
whatToWatch: Further updates to the total as more drained wallets are identified
Any fix or guidance issued to affected users
questions: Why does this tally differ from other outlets' running totals?
Is there a clear end in sight to the draining?

sources.title: Coldcard Bitcoin Exploit Balloons to $88 Million as Attackers Keep Draining Wallets

stories.title: Trump Media sells another 2,628 BTC, trimming holdings to 4,261 BTC
stories.summary: Trump Media sold an additional 2,628 BTC from its treasury, according to Cointelegraph, reducing its total Bitcoin holdings to 4,261 BTC. No reason for the sale was given in the report.
stories.whyItMatters: It marks a notable scale-back of a high-profile public company's Bitcoin treasury position, relevant context for tracking corporate BTC holding trends.
whatToWatch: Whether further sales reduce holdings further
Any company statement on the use of proceeds
questions: What prompted the sale, and is more selling planned?

stories.title: Coldcard hack drives biggest sub-1 BTC transaction wave since FTX: CryptoQuant
stories.summary: Analytics firm CryptoQuant found that the Coldcard hack has triggered the largest volume of sub-1 BTC transactions since the FTX collapse, according to Cointelegraph. It's an early read on the exploit's on-chain footprint, ahead of later reports that raised the total funds affected.
stories.whyItMatters: Unusual spikes in small-denomination transaction volume can be an early on-chain signature of a security incident, useful for analysts trying to gauge its true scale.
whatToWatch: Whether the sub-1 BTC transaction volume keeps climbing
How this data reconciles with later dollar-value estimates of the exploit
questions: Does this reflect attacker structuring of funds or affected users simply moving small balances?

sources.title: Coldcard hack sparks biggest sub-1 BTC move since FTX: CryptoQuant
